title: An Execution‑Oriented Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Simulate→Rollback Pipelines for LLM‑Assisted NetOps: a Confirmatory Study with gpt‑5‑mini
abstract: We preregistered (c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1) and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to test whether a guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline reduces actionable misconfigurations relative to a generation‑only baseline on vendor‑neutral NetOps tasks. Design: N=160 vendor‑neutral tasks (routing/ACL/NAT), model=gpt‑5‑mini, shared_initial_generation (one generated candidate per task reused across conditions), deterministic simulator adjudicator, primary estimand = paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion, analysis = paired bootstrap (10,000, seed=1729) and McNemar exact. Result: baseline actionable = 0/160; guarded actionable = 0/160; paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]); McNemar p = 1.00. The preregistered target (≥30% relative reduction) is unevaluable here because the shared_initial_generation pairing created a ceiling effect: the single shared candidate per task was non‑actionable for all tasks, leaving no headroom for the guarded pipeline to demonstrate benefit. We release SHA‑256‑verified artifacts and provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of this confirmatory design failure and prescriptive recommendations for informative follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Motivation and problem statement. Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed for NetOps tasks that translate intent into configuration and propose changes that, if enacted, must be operationally safe. Prior work emphasises verifier‑ or simulator‑assisted pipelines (generate→validate→repair) to reduce misconfiguration enactments (e.g., VeriFlow and recent LLM→NetOps pipelines). We selected a narrow, preregistered confirmatory question: does a guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline (C) reduce the actionable misconfiguration rate by ≥30% relative to a generation‑only baseline (A) on a representative vendor‑neutral NetOps task set? We preregistered the full experiment (c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1) and executed it with fully archived artifacts. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, deterministic execution with complete artifact hashing and per‑task scoring; (2) publication of exact numeric outcomes and representative scoring JSON hashes; (3) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the preregistered contrast became unevaluable in this run and concise experimental prescriptions for informative follow‑ups. The final paragraph below previews the empirical outcome: all shared generated candidates were adjudicated non‑actionable by the deterministic simulator (baseline = 0/160), producing a ceiling effect that rendered the preregistered primary contrast unevaluable.
sections.related_work: NetOps verification and generate→validate architectures. Real‑time and offline verification tools (VeriFlow and successors) provide fast invariant checks of forwarding state; generate→validate→repair architectures have been proposed to mitigate LLM hallucinations in configuration synthesis. Recent surveys and benchmarks (OpsEval, LogEval, MeshAgent, MNC, Flow‑of‑Action) emphasise workflow‑centric evaluation, constraint encoding, and simulator‑backed adjudication. Our work differs by (a) preregistering a paired, execution‑oriented estimand, (b) freezing a precise generation policy (shared_initial_generation) to control generator variance, and (c) publishing complete, SHA‑256‑verified artifacts that permit deterministic reanalysis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. Study id: c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1. Task corpus: N=160 vendor‑neutral tasks partitioned into routing (~64), ACL (~64), NAT/other (~32). Tasks were selected deterministically from public vendor‑neutral collections and augmented using preregistered seeds [42,123,999]; selection scripts and hashes are archived. Model and adapter: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Generation policy (preregistered): shared_initial_generation — one generated candidate per task produced once and reused for both baseline and guarded conditions to eliminate generator variance. Guarded pipeline (C): candidate → constraint validator → deterministic simulator enactment → rollback candidate if simulator flags actionable; baseline (A): generation only (same shared candidate) with no validator/simulator gating. Adjudication: deterministic simulator produces an actionable boolean per candidate (actionable=true implies configuration would be blocked in a safe deployment). Primary estimand: paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion (P_actionable_A − P_actionable_C) across N=160 paired tasks. Analysis: paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for 95% CI and McNemar exact two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes. Stopping/retry: full planned run (no early stopping); up to two transient retries for provider errors. Artifact integrity: all raw outputs, provider call logs, per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), and analysis scripts are archived and SHA‑256 hashed (see Disclosure for representative hashes).
sections.results: Execution summary and primary outcomes. Execution completed as preregistered: planned episodes 320 (160 tasks × 2 conditions) and completed episodes 320. Because of shared_initial_generation, provider model calls used = 160 (one generation per task). Primary, artifact‑verified outcomes: baseline actionable = 0/160; guarded actionable = 0/160; paired difference (A − C) = 0.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact p = 1.00. The per‑task contingency table is n_11 = 160 (both non‑actionable), n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0. Representative per‑task evidentiary pointers (each scoring JSON is archived and SHA‑256 hashed in the execution manifest): task‑000001 baseline scoring JSON (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json) SHA‑256 = e321b84c41233594d2bebc0d01722cade9ab148516fcf13fd9788c94fb638e59 → actionable=false; task‑000050 baseline scoring JSON = e4fa1208479e3d51adbdb7147ea951766fda52baefee705d2320da8870395d90 → actionable=false; task‑000160 baseline scoring JSON = 6310438573e09696982a7edd299d12731966266bd66fb1470123f0b1549ba8ef → actionable=false. Deterministic reconciliation checks passed: pair accounting, episode accounting, and provider call audit are consistent with the preregistered shared‑generation policy (execution manifest contains full call_cache and provider_call records and their hashes).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and diagnosis. The observed degenerate outcome arises from the preregistered shared_initial_generation policy combined with a permissive generator for the chosen tasks: producing one candidate per task and reusing it across conditions intentionally removed generator variance, but when that shared candidate is non‑actionable under the deterministic simulator, the guarded pipeline has no opportunity to block or repair anything—producing a ceiling effect (n_11=160). This run therefore provides no evidence for or against the operational value of guarded pipelines in general; it documents a confirmatory design failure mode. Practical design lessons (artifact‑grounded): (1) calibration is required before locking confirmatory designs: ensure the baseline actionable rate > 0 (headroom) or permit independent per‑condition generation; (2) if the hypothesis concerns downstream pipeline interventions, use independent per‑condition generations (one generation per task per condition) rather than shared reuse; (3) validate the simulator predicate against a human‑adjudicated sample to detect overly permissive or overly strict adjudication semantics. Recommendations for future confirmatory runs (implementable from archived artifacts): run a small calibration sample (e.g., 20 tasks) to estimate baseline actionability; switch to independent per‑condition generation when testing pipeline interventions; or select adversarial or historically‑unsafe tasks to ensure detectable baseline risk.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, fully archived paired confirmatory experiment comparing generation‑only and guarded generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipelines using gpt‑5‑mini on N=160 vendor‑neutral NetOps tasks. Observed baseline actionable = 0/160 and guarded actionable = 0/160; paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.00). The preregistered shared_initial_generation design produced a ceiling effect that made the preregistered ≥30% relative‑reduction target unevaluable in this run. The principal scientific value of this execution is (a) full determinism and reproducibility—SHA‑256‑verified artifacts permit deterministic reanalysis—and (b) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of a common confirmatory design failure mode. We publish the execution manifest, per‑task scoring JSONs (with hashes), and analysis artifacts and recommend calibrated independent‑generation confirmatory designs when the guarded pipeline's operational value is to be tested.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).

Models and orchestration: primary model = gpt‑5‑mini (hosted API). Orchestration/adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The Master Prompt bundle guiding the autonomous run is the Master Prompt v1 — Autonomous CNSM 2026 Research Run; the Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development. Pre‑lock development: collaborative pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred and were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence. Autonomy claim: after the autonomy lock, literature review, research‑gap selection, preregistration, prompt generation, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, manuscript drafting, and revision were performed autonomously. No human manually edited the technical manuscript content, numerical results, figures, captions, references, or this Disclosure Statement after the autonomy lock.

Preregistration and frozen design: the run followed preregistration id c1_exec_benchmark_2026_prereg_v1 which froze the confirmatory paired design, task selection (N=160; augmentation seeds [42,123,999]), shared_initial_generation policy (one candidate per task reused across baseline and guarded), model (gpt‑5‑mini), maximum model calls (320), primary estimand, analysis plan (paired bootstrap 10,000, seed=1729 and McNemar exact), retry policy, and stopping rules. No post‑hoc changes affecting confirmatory inference were made.

Artifact integrity and reproducibility: all raw model outputs, provider call logs, canonicalized configurations, per‑task scoring JSONs, deterministic simulator scoring schema, analysis scripts, and the execution manifest are archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Representative authoritative files and their SHA‑256 values (as recorded in the execution manifest) include: execution/raw_results.jsonl = 2445d0f8e9be9cfa34ede1bbe80b82d6f05b51bcafc7c1688d0ed8e1c73d8044; execution/result_schema.json = 63199db3f7219b969acc5497fae613c8d5df16e081768969f67b7b3024844465; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv = fba3b0ca21c7c7c380ed1134b4fce48b0870bf72a7be0fd8610bf7e6b63a970b. Per‑task scoring JSONs are under execution/scoring/ and are enumerated with SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest; those scoring files contain the actionable flag used for primary inference. Example scoring JSON hashes (artifacts used in manuscript text): execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json = e321b84c41233594d2bebc0d01722cade9ab148516fcf13fd9788c94fb638e59; execution/scoring/task-000050-baseline.json = e4fa1208479e3d51adbdb7147ea951766fda52baefee705d2320da8870395d90; execution/scoring/task-000160-baseline.json = 6310438573e09696982a7edd299d12731966266bd66fb1470123f0b1549ba8ef.

Provider calls and retries: planned maximum model calls = 320; actual provider model calls used = 160 because the preregistered shared_initial_generation design used one generation per task. The preregistered retry policy allowed up to two transient retries for provider errors; none materially affected confirmatory outcomes. Provider call audit, call cache entries, and their hashes are recorded in the execution manifest.

Human role limitations: the Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock development. After the autonomy lock, no human performed manual edits to technical content or numeric results. The artifacts and hashes above permit deterministic verification of the run without additional manual manuscript edits.
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline generation produced zero actionable misconfigurations under the chosen deterministic simulator (baseline = 0/160), making the preregistered ≥30% relative‑reduction target unevaluable.

Shared‑candidate policy: the preregistered shared_initial_generation (one candidate per task used for both baseline and guarded) prevents the guarded pipeline from demonstrating benefit on tasks where the shared candidate is already non‑actionable.
Single‑model scope: conclusions apply to gpt‑5‑mini and the exact prompts/call budget used; multi‑model generality is unresolved.
Construct abstraction: the deterministic simulator predicate is an abstraction and may not capture all production failure modes; a small human adjudication check is recommended for production claims.
No live device enactment: evaluation used a deterministic simulator rather than live device enactment, limiting external validity to production rollouts.
